title: The Morning Brief: Owners ratify record Seahawks sale as it awaits September close
dek: NFL owners unanimously approved the record $9.612 billion Seahawks sale on Wednesday, with the deal expected to close in September, while MLB's union rejected the league's free agency compression proposal and WNBA ratings hit a 29-year high.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The NFL's Seahawks sale and MLB's labor proposal both moved forward today, but neither is finished: the Seahawks deal awaits a September close and a Khosla family divestiture, while MLB and its union remain far apart with December 1 approaching.
bottom_line: NFL owners unanimously ratified the record $9.612 billion Seahawks sale, but the deal is expected to close in September and still requires the Khosla family to divest a 49ers stake. MLB's union rejected the league's proposal to compress free agency to three weeks and freeze transactions for a month, leaving both sides entrenched with the Dec. 1 CBA expiration approaching. The day's common thread is decisions rendered without finality: approvals, charges, and requests that advance matters rather than close them, from the Jacobs charges to the SEC eligibility injunction to Hellebuyck's trade request. The reporting is clear on what each party has decided or proposed but does not resolve what happens next in any of these threads. Watch Friday's Hillsborough County stadium vote, the Seahawks' September closing timeline, and the next moves in MLB's labor talks as the clearest near-term tests.
body: The day's clearest thread is approval without finality. NFL owners voted unanimously Wednesday to ratify the $9.612 billion sale of the Seahawks to a group led by Vinod Khosla's family, a league record, but the deal is expected to close in September 2026 and the Khosla family must still divest a minority stake in the 49ers to comply with league rules. MLB sent the players union a formal proposal to compress free agency into a 2-3 week window in December followed by a monthlong transaction freeze, and the union rejected it the same day, calling it an elimination of player rights. A federal judge in Dallas issued a temporary restraining order blocking the SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey from overturning an injunction on college eligibility for players with NFL contract time, leaving the underlying dispute open. Each of these stories reached a decision point today without reaching an end point.

Alongside those institutional moves, the day carried a heavy transactions and injury docket. The Aces will be without forward NaLyssa Smith for the rest of the regular season after a non-contact leg injury, with Las Vegas sitting third in the standings, one-half game ahead of Atlanta, as the team navigates a hard cap that currently blocks a hardship exception. DeWanna Bonner signed with the Atlanta Dream after a Phoenix Mercury buyout, joining Angel Reese for the playoff stretch. Jonathan Kuminga signed a two-year, $13 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves using the taxpayer mid-level exception, settling a second consecutive slow free agency. The Rams traded running back Jarquez Hunter to the Dolphins for receiver Tutu Atwell, who returns to the team that drafted him. The Giants placed receiver Calvin Austin on injured reserve after a torn ACL in training camp. And Connor Hellebuyck, a three-time Vezina Trophy winner, publicly requested a trade from the Winnipeg Jets, a move his full no-movement clause lets him control.

Legal and disciplinary matters ran in parallel. Packers running back Josh Jacobs was formally charged with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property after Brown County prosecutors declined to pursue a felony strangulation charge from his May arrest. CBS broadcaster Tony Romo faces three citations, including first-offense operating while intoxicated, from a July 23 Wisconsin arrest, and remains indefinitely suspended from CBS's No. 1 booth. UEFA filed discovery motions in three U.S. federal courts targeting FIFA, president Gianni Infantino, Thrive Capital, and Greg Maffei, seeking documents to support anticipated criminal charges against Infantino in Switzerland. None of these matters reached resolution today; each names a next procedural step.

On the field and track, the Sky-Fever game on NBC and Peacock drew 3.31 million viewers, the WNBA's most-watched regular-season game since the league's opening weekend in 1997, with Caitlin Clark's 37 points and Kelsey Mitchell's 30 combining for 67 of Indiana's total in a 113-90 win. The broadcast also included the ejection of Enes Kanter Freedom from Wintrust Arena after an altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud, with eyewitness accounts of the incident differing. Unrivaled announced a Series C round valuing the women's 3-on-3 league at $650 million, nearly double its September 2025 valuation, with players retaining a 30% ownership stake. At the Diamond League final in Zurich, Alison dos Santos ran 45.80 seconds in the 400m hurdles and Masai Russell ran 12.09 seconds in the women's 100m hurdles, both world records set the same evening.

The reporting does not explain why MLB and the union remain this far apart beyond the stated positions: MLB's spokesman framed the proposal as tied to a salary cap system that would improve roster stability, while the union's interim executive director said the proposal would reduce player compensation and leverage. Similarly, the reporting does not detail what triggered the Freedom-Cloud altercation beyond conflicting accounts from the team owner and a courtside witness.
Desk boards were not available this run, so the figures above rely on the day's reported stories rather than a current league tape.

The coming days carry several concrete checkpoints. Tampa's Hillsborough County commission votes Friday on the Rays' $2.36 billion stadium deal after the city council's narrow 4-3 approval. The Seahawks sale is expected to close in September 2026, with the Khosla family's required divestiture of its 49ers stake to watch in the meantime. MLB's Dec. 1 CBA expiration approaches with the union's rejection setting up further bargaining, and any lockout would follow that date. The SEC's college eligibility dispute continues toward the Protect College Sports Act in the Senate. And Caitlin Clark, listed probable for Friday's game against Connecticut with an ongoing back issue, plays before a weeks-long WNBA break for the FIBA Women's World Cup.
